pages.text: "I'll take out all the pinecones!" Yuki tipped the basket onto the porch. Pinecones rolled everywhere. The empty basket was pushed to the edge.
"I'll make a mountain and play tomorrow and the day after!" Yuki stood, laid, and rolled the cones. Brown dog Momo napped beneath the porch.
Getting up for water, Yuki stepped on a pinecone and slipped, landing on their bottom. "Ouch! Who put that there?"
The biggest pinecone was missing, too. Not under the cushion or beneath the porch. Yuki pouted.
Grandma pushed the empty basket in front of Yuki. "The pinecones' home is here, but no one's gone inside." Yuki stared at it.
Yuki picked them up one at a time. Tap, tap, tap. The basket filled, and the porch grew clearer.
At last, the biggest pinecone came out of a gap in the threshold. "Found it! You hid here! After Playing, Into the Basket!"
The porch was clear and smooth. Even running would not make Yuki slip now. Momo climbed up and flopped down. The full basket waited at the edge.
The next day, Yuki paused during play and fixed the scarf knot. "One, after playing, to the basket! Two, put them in one by one! Three, basket back at the porch's edge!"
Yuki raised the big pinecone, and Grandma patted their back. Putting things in a basket brought missing things back, too. "After Playing, Into the Basket!"
